properties.statement: FIELD EVIDENCE FROM A FULL DAY OF 3 BOSSES + 4 WORKERS ON ONE `--shared` GRAPH: WHAT HELD, RECORDED SO IT IS NOT TRADED AWAY WHILE FIXING WHAT DID NOT. Peak concurrency measured: 7 `--shared` client processes plus 1 `--serve-shared`, across 3 boss seats and 4 worker sessions over ~5 hours (dev_storyflow, 2026-08-07, api-boss `5d608b85`, written from a live shift rather than from docs). The reporter asked for these to be stated BEFORE the complaints. (1) ZERO LOCK CONTENTION, not one instance, all day. This is the headline. Under the old stdio/exclusive-RocksDB behaviour a second session was SILENTLY BLINDED, and their PROTOCOL literally instructed workers NOT to run reflow2. Seven sessions read AND wrote concurrently with nobody blocked, queued or blinded — and the `REFLOW2-HOLD`/`RELEASE` ritual they used to run on the boss channel is simply GONE. A whole coordination protocol deleted, not merely eased. (2) SERVER-SIDE BEHAVIOUR REACHES EVERY ATTACHED SESSION WITH NO RESTART. When the server rolled to 0.24.0 the fixed detectors reached all attached seats MID-SESSION — one seat watched defects 42 -> 6 happen live in its own tool output. Only the TOOL LIST is negotiated at connect, so a session needs restarting ONLY if it needs a genuinely new tool. Measured consequence: they restarted 1 session instead of 6 and five kept their context. The reporter calls this major, non-obvious, and asks that it be kept and documented loudly. (3) `claim_region` BEING ADVISORY RATHER THAN A LOCK IS THE RIGHT CALL and they explicitly defend it: it makes overlap visible without inventing a blocking primitive; nobody deadlocked, nobody waited on a peer, and no claim ever had to be force-released after a session died. A lock would have recreated the exact problem `--shared` just solved. (4) `mint_seat` + `add_contributor` AS SEPARATE CONCEPTS held up once the roles were clear — seat = this session for claim_region, contributor = durable authorship. (5) CONCURRENT READS OF THE SAME NODES WERE COMPLETELY UNEVENTFUL, including reading nodes while workers wrote elsewhere — no staleness, no error, no surprise. (6) WORKERS RUNNING THE DESIGN BRAIN CHANGED THE QUALITY OF THEIR REPORTS: findings came back as graph evidence with node ids the boss could re-resolve, instead of prose that had to be taken on trust. THEIR EXPLICIT 'WHAT NOT TO CHANGE' LIST: advisory-not-lock claims; the refusal to accept an artifact checksum silently (design_holds vs design_updated vs baseline_established called a genuinely good forced question); per-property merge; skills served rather than installed, so they never go stale in a repo; and `--shared` itself.
